places.text: Mountain gorillas in Bwindi, chimpanzees in Kibale, and tree-climbing lions in the Ishasha sector.
places.title: Wildlife Encounters

places.text: Kob on the Kasenyi plains, elephant on the Kazinga Channel, and Kidepo Valley with almost nobody in it.
places.title: Queen Elizabeth and Kidepo

places.text: Uganda's kingdoms were never abolished for long — Buganda, Bunyoro and Toro still hold court.
places.title: The Kingdom of Buganda

places.text: The Batwa, forest people of the southwest, and the Karamojong cattle-keepers of the northeast plains.
places.title: Batwa and Karamojong

places.text: The Bagisu Imbalu season in the east, and four days of music on the banks of the Nile at Jinja.
places.title: Imbalu and Nyege Nyege

places.text: Bark cloth from the mutuba fig, made in Buganda for six hundred years and now UNESCO-listed.
places.title: Bark Cloth and Basketry

places.text: The boda boda is the transport system; Owino market is where the whole city goes to buy everything.
places.title: Boda Bodas and Owino

places.text: Crater lakes around Fort Portal, papyrus swamp on the Nile, and the Rwenzori snowline sitting on the equator.
places.title: Green, End to End

places.text: The Rwenzori range holds glaciers three degrees from the equator, and Margherita Peak at 5,109 m.
places.title: The Mountains of the Moon

places.text: The entire Victoria Nile forced through a seven-metre gap and dropped forty-three metres into the gorge below.
places.title: Murchison, Through the Gap

places.text: The Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja; Lake Bunyonyi holds twenty-nine islands and no bilharzia.
places.title: Where the Nile Begins

places.text: Freshwater beaches and fishing villages on Lake Victoria, an hour and a half by ferry from Entebbe.
places.title: The Ssese Islands

places.text: Thirteen primate species in Kibale, and in Bwindi a forest so old and so thick it was never logged.
places.title: Kibale and Bwindi

places.text: White-water rafting below the source at Jinja, plus bungee, kayaking and the long walk up Sipi.
places.title: Grade Five on the Nile

places.text: Steamed green banana with groundnut sauce, chicken cooked in banana leaf, and an egg rolled in a chapati on every corner.
places.title: Rolex, Matoke, Luwombo

places.text: The burial ground of four Buganda kings, thatched, enormous and rebuilt by the clans who have always maintained it.
places.title: The Kasubi Tombs

places.text: Royal drums, regalia and clan structures that survived the protectorate, the 1966 crisis and the 1970s.
places.title: Kingdoms Still Standing

places.text: A capital built across hills and traffic, with the Gaddafi Mosque minaret giving the best view of all of it.
places.title: Kampala on Seven Hills

places.text: The Uganda National Mosque, the Namirembe and Rubaga cathedrals facing each other across two hills.
places.title: Minaret, Dome and Thatch

places.text: Community walks in Buhoma and Nkuringo, run by the villages that share the forest with the gorillas.
places.title: Villages at the Forest Edge

places.text: Three waterfalls and a coffee walk at Sipi, then the long crater rim of Mount Elgon above it.
places.title: Sipi, Elgon, Bisoke

places.text: Small lodges on the Bwindi ridge and the Kazinga Channel, close enough to walk to the trailhead after breakfast.
places.title: Lodges at the Forest Edge

places.text: Permit revenue funds the park and pays a share to the parishes around it — which is why the gorilla numbers are rising.
places.title: The Gorilla Permit

places.text: The Ndali-Kasenda crater field before the haze lifts, and the Ishasha fig trees in the late afternoon.
places.title: Crater Lakes at First Light

places.text: The furthest park from Kampala and the emptiest: Narus valley, the Morungole range, and cheetah nobody photographs.
places.title: Kidepo Valley

places.text: Nowhere else puts gorillas, chimpanzees, the Big Five, a snowline and the Nile within one week of driving.
places.title: Half the World's Gorillas
